claims.claim: SEO is framed as search-everywhere optimization, with traditional search retained for traffic and AI retrieval infrastructure.
AI answers are separated into static-corpus knowledge and current web/RAG retrieval.
Google AI products and independent AI platforms are separate observation surfaces because answers and citations vary.
Local visibility depends on GBP/local-pack performance plus third-party sources used by non-Google systems.
Ecommerce and social platforms become vertical search branches; topical consistency is emphasized within each channel.
Traditional and AI search form the universal core, with local, ecommerce, social, and other surfaces activated by vertical fit.
Traditional rank, AI citation, and brand mention coverage are distinct states that can diverge.
The goal set includes ranking owned pages, ranking external properties, commercial-query brand mentions, becoming a retrieval source, and appearing on top retrieval sources.
Video scripts should state the target topic clearly because transcripts are machine-readable retrieval material.
Distribution should target platforms already visible for the query rather than defaulting to every channel.
One-URL SEO is insufficient; agent execution requires a strategy and skills iterated against real outputs.
Agentic execution needs persistence and checkpoints because long browser jobs can crash and lose work.
Practitioner process knowledge and a systemized SOP/skill environment are presented as the bottleneck to effective execution.
Unlinked brand mentions on recurring retrieval-source sites can influence AI answers.
claims.boundary: No independent experiment receipt in the source.
